newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN INTERBANK RATE ENDS UP DESPITE FUND INJECT.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN INTERBANK RATE ENDS UP DESPITE FUND INJECT.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate ended higher on Thursday on tight liquidity, despite fund injection by the central bank, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate, which has soared more than two percentage points since August 2, finished at 8.862 percent against Wednesday's 8.748 percent, well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
Dealers said the T$8 billion worth of funds injected into the banking system through open market operations was not large enough to ease liquidity during the peak of routine monthly payroll demand.

The bank executed a repurchase of negotiable certificates of deposit offered by interested financial institutions with a rate of 8.00-8.25 percent. The institutions have the option of repurchasing the NCDs in five days' time.
Banking system's accumulated reserve excess has shown a negative T$245.2 billion since the beginning of the current reserve period.

Dealers said the government's five-day auction of some 418 million shares in Chiao Tung Bank, which began on Monday, was expected to further siphon some T$30 billion in liquidity out of the banking system.

Strong intervention orchestrated by the central bank also offset the bank's fund injection move, dealers said, adding the bank had sold at least US$180 million in the foreign exchange market near close of trade to defend the local unit.
This enabled the Taiwan dollar to reel back from the low of T$28.97 to settle at T$28.639, they said.

The 30-day commercial paper closed slightly lower at 8.50 percent from Wednesday 8.75 close on a general expectation that the central bank would inject large amount of funds to ease liquidity, dealers said.
In the bond market, the benchmark 86/4 bond yield was at 6.135 percent against Wednesday's 6.14 percent.
